questions.description: How does adding endurance training affect muscle hypertrophy?
questions.gap: Whole-muscle and fiber outcomes differ; trained runner dose and region-specific effects remain unresolved.

questions.description: How does the scheduling of resistance and endurance sessions affect outcomes?
questions.gap: No validated individual spacing interval or optimal weekly layout.

questions.description: How does same-session ordering affect concurrent adaptations?
questions.gap: Run-priority and dual-trained comparisons remain limited.

questions.description: How does supplemental strength training affect running economy?
questions.gap: Incremental benefit of additional work in already strong runners remains unknown.

questions.description: How does supplemental strength training affect running performance?
questions.gap: Race-specific effects and optimal strength dose in dual-trained runners remain unknown.

questions.description: How does adding resistance training affect aerobic capacity during endurance training?
questions.gap: VO2max retention is not equivalent to running performance retention.

claims.assertion: Pooled explosive-strength gains were smaller with concurrent training than with resistance training alone.
claims.limitations: Mixed modalities and experience; influential study and sensitivity of subgroup estimates; not maximal strength.
claims.assessment: 18 studies; moderate methodological limitations; running-specific and individual transfer unresolved.

support.restriction: Explosive strength only; no individual spacing threshold.

claims.assertion: The average whole-muscle hypertrophy difference between concurrent training and matched resistance-only training was close to zero.
claims.limitations: 15 studies; heterogeneous protocols, mixed experience, no equivalence test; fiber-level outcome differs.
claims.assessment: Pooled contrast moderately precise; running dose and dual-trained transfer unestablished.

claims.assertion: The estimated concurrent-versus-strength-only contrast for lower-body strength differed between male and female subgroups.
claims.limitations: Sparse female data, wide female interval and study-level moderation; no causal individual sex-specific policy.
claims.assessment: 20 lower-body studies; unclear concealment/detection bias; directness limited.

support.result: Male SMD −0.43 (95% CI −0.64 to −0.22); female 0.08 (−0.34 to 0.49); subgroup difference p=0.03.
support.restriction: Comparison of program effects across sex strata; not a sex-based progression rule.

claims.assertion: The synthesis did not detect a difference in the concurrent-training lower-body strength effect between strength-trained and untrained subgroups.
claims.limitations: Study-level classification; insufficient highly trained data; no equivalence or evidence of absence.
claims.assessment: 16 studies in this moderation contrast; related Petré subgroup result uses different classifications and inclusion.

support.result: Between-strength-experience subgroup p=1.00; subgroup estimate intervals not extracted in this record.
support.restriction: Interaction result only; not a within-trained comparison.

claims.assertion: The pooled fiber-level hypertrophy estimate modestly favored resistance-only training, with uncertainty reaching zero at reported precision.
claims.limitations: Only three running studies; biopsy variation, mixed populations and substantial heterogeneity; not whole-muscle hypertrophy.
claims.assessment: 15 studies, mean PEDro 4.3; related source protocol and potential overlap with Schumann.

support.restriction: Overall fiber-level outcome; not a body-composition prediction.

claims.assertion: In the running subgroup, type I fiber hypertrophy was smaller with concurrent training than with resistance-only training.
claims.limitations: Only three running studies overall; §3.3 reports no statistically significant subgroup differences; no proof of running-versus-cycling effect modification.
claims.assessment: Small subgroup, heterogeneity, study-level modality assignment; no approved transfer.

support.restriction: Type I fibers, not whole-muscle hypertrophy or a mandate to replace running.

claims.assertion: In the trained same-session subgroup, the estimate favored resistance-only training for lower-body 1RM.
claims.limitations: Study-level subgroup; same-session definition under 20 min; overall review duration range; not direct randomized comparison of timing.
claims.assessment: Small studies and mixed running/cycling; differences in dose and training status.

support.restriction: Not evidence of a minimum safe gap.

claims.assertion: In the trained different-session subgroup, the lower-body 1RM contrast was uncertain and close to zero.
claims.limitations: Study-level subgroup; separate defined as over two hours; overall review duration range; interval allows meaningful impairment.
claims.assessment: No equivalence test or direct timing contrast.

support.restriction: No inference about intermediate spacing or individual recovery time.

claims.assertion: Resistance-first ordering yielded greater lower-body dynamic strength improvement in the pooled same-session comparisons.
claims.limitations: Mostly recreational/untrained samples, varied modalities; not a race-specific performance or separate-day ordering result.
claims.assessment: Direct sequence contrast but limited dual-trained running applicability.

support.result: Weighted mean difference in percent change 6.91 percentage points (95% CI 1.96 to 11.87).
support.restriction: Only this outcome; no universal order.

claims.assertion: The pooled running-economy contrast favored the studied supplemental strength method over control.
claims.limitations: Varied control conditions and lifting experience; speed-dependent tests; no individual conversion to race time.
claims.assessment: Publisher results and review certainty assessment; dual-trained marginal effect unknown. Horizon is review overall.

support.restriction: Negative effect favors lower measured running cost. Study prescriptions are not defaults.

claims.assertion: The pooled running-economy contrast favored the studied supplemental strength method over control.
claims.limitations: Heterogeneity and outlier sensitivity, distinct method combinations; no head-to-head superiority.
claims.assessment: Publisher results and review certainty assessment; dual-trained marginal effect unknown. Horizon is review overall.

support.restriction: Negative effect favors lower measured running cost. Study prescriptions are not defaults.

claims.assertion: The pooled running-performance contrast favored the studied supplemental strength method over control.
claims.limitations: Combines time trials and TTE; no individual race-time percentage or optimal additional strength dose.
claims.assessment: Mixed laboratory/field outcomes and overlapping primary studies; hybrid transfer not approved. Horizon is review overall.

support.restriction: Negative effects favor supplemental strength; no predicted individual race-time change.

claims.assertion: The pooled running-performance contrast favored the studied supplemental strength method over control.
claims.limitations: Heterogeneous combined methods; no direct proof of superiority to high-load-only training.
claims.assessment: Mixed laboratory/field outcomes and overlapping primary studies; hybrid transfer not approved. Horizon is review overall.

support.restriction: Negative effects favor supplemental strength; no predicted individual race-time change.

claims.assertion: In the trial, the supplemented group improved oxygen cost at the end of the prolonged run relative to running-only control.
claims.limitations: Male runners, 14 per group; abstract-level extraction; combined stimulus; baseline strength training and CIs require full-text confirmation.
claims.assessment: Randomized comparison and explicit time-specific outcome; no independent full-text or rights review.

support.result: Change −2.1% vs +0.6%, p=0.04; group×training×run-time p=0.003, partial eta-squared 0.13.
support.restriction: Measured laboratory oxygen cost at 90 minutes; not race performance or a universal training dose.

claims.assertion: The trained endurance subgroup did not show detectably smaller VO2max gains with concurrent versus endurance-only training.
claims.limitations: Mixed aerobic modes and sparse high-level evidence; no equivalence test; not running economy, race time or retention.
claims.assessment: Outcome-specific comparison with moderate imprecision; study-level training-status classification.

support.restriction: Trained endurance subgroup only; no inference about all performance qualities.

relations.subject: separate-session-trained-lower-body-strength@1
relations.reason: Same review, distinct timing strata and common comparator type. Separate-session estimate is uncertain; this does not estimate a randomized direct timing contrast or establish a minimum gap.

relations.subject: concurrent-strength-experience-moderation@1
relations.reason: Huiberts did not detect a strength-status interaction; Petré reports a within-trained program comparison. Different estimands and classification, overlapping literature; neither logically refutes the other.

relations.subject: pooled-concurrent-fiber-hypertrophy@1
relations.reason: Different tissue measurement levels and partially overlapping research; do not transfer whole-muscle estimate to fibers or vice versa.

methods.question: concurrent-timing
methods.description: Compare feasible weekly schedules with explicit key-session priorities and actual athlete responses; consider separation or ordering changes before altering protected dose.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 003 CT-P02 v0.2; original candidate programming method, not empirical finding.
methods.tradeoffs: Spacing, adherence and other priorities can conflict; no universal interval; direct timing evidence limited.

methods.question: strength-running-economy
methods.description: Map existing resistance training to running and strength objectives before adding supplemental work; consider retaining suitable strength exposure or replacing less important work.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 003 CT-P04; original candidate programming method, not empirical finding.
methods.tradeoffs: Additional work may not improve running in already strong athletes and may compromise session quality; exact doses unvalidated.

methods.question: concurrent-strength
methods.description: Review both disciplines and secondary commitments within a shared block; compare feasible alternatives, disclose uncertainty and require athlete approval for objective changes.
methods.provenance: Research Packet 003 HP-P01 and CT-P05; original candidate programming method, not empirical finding.
methods.tradeoffs: No demonstrated optimal priority trajectory or adaptation algorithm; needs athlete preferences, nutrition context and explicit secondary protection.
